result.markdown: --- format: html: toc: false --- ## Welcome These are the materials for the _Practical Machine Learning with tidymodels_ workshop to be hosted at the [posit::conf(2026)](https://posit.co/blog/workshops-at-positconf2026). [tidymodels](https://www.tidymodels.org/) is a complete framework that implements modeling best practices using [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) principles. Led by [Max Kuhn](https://max-kuhn.org/) and [Emil Hvitfeldt](https://emilhvitfeldt.com/), this workshop will teach you core tidymodels packages to preprocess data, specify and train models, and optimize the tuning parameter. You'll learn tidymodels syntax as well as the process of predictive modeling for tabular data. Time permitting, you'll be introduced to basic pre-processing with recipes. ## Is this workshop for me? This workshop is for you if you: - are comfortable using tidyverse packages to read data into R, transform and reshape data, and make a variety of graphs, and - have some experience with modeling, such as linear regression, logistic regression, or tree-based models. While the workshop will teach some terminology and modeling philosophy, it is primarily focused on showing users how to effectively develop, iterate, and validate a machine learning model. ## Preparation Please join the workshop with a computer that has the following installed (all available for free): - A recent version of R, available at - A recent version of an IDE, either - RStudio Desktop (RStudio Desktop Open Source License, at least v2024.04.0), available at or - Positron, available at - For the _core slides_ (decks 1-9), the following R packages can be installed from the R console: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Packages for the core materials # fmt: skip pkgs_core <- c("dimRed", "embed", "extrasteps", "future", "igraph", "mirai", "parallelly", "probably", "RANN", "ranger", "RcppML", "rpart.plot", "splines2", "tidymodels", "xgboost") install.packages(pkgs_core) ``` ::: - One core package, [almanac](https://davisvaughan.github.io/almanac/), was archived from CRAN on 2026-08-22, so it has to be installed from GitHub: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages("pak") pak::pak("davisvaughan/almanac") ``` ::: - For the _extra slides_, you'll also need: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Additional packages for the extra materials # fmt: skip pkgs_extras <- c("bonsai", "brulee", "Cubist", "desirability2", "earth", "finetune", "important", "kknn", "lightgbm", "lme4", "rules", "stacks") install.packages(pkgs_extras) ``` ::: If you plan to run the postprocessing or iterative search slides, `brulee` also needs a one-time torch download: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} torch::install_torch() ``` ::: Also, you should make sure that you have installed the newest version of a few packages. To check this, you can run the following code snippet. It will also prompt you to install the required versions if they are not already installed. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rlang::check_installed("tidymodels", version = "1.5.0") rlang::check_installed("modeldata", version = "1.6.0") ``` ::: A few slides mention alternatives that need extra packages. You only need these if you want to work through those specific exercises: `rstanarm` (for `embed::step_lencode_bayes()`), `partykit` (for the conditional inference tree engine in deck 03), and `usethis` (only if you download the materials with `usethis::use_course()`). If you're a Windows user and encounter an error message during installation noting a missing Rtools installation, install Rtools using the installer linked [here](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/). ## Slides These slides are designed to use with live teaching and are published for workshop participants' convenience. They are not meant as standalone learning materials. For that, we recommend [tidymodels.org](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/) and [*Tidy Modeling with R*](https://www.tmwr.org/). - 01: [Introduction](slides/01-introduction.html){target="_blank"} - 02: [Your data budget](slides/02-data-budget.html){target="_blank"} - 03: [What makes a model?](slides/03-what-makes-a-model.html){target="_blank"} - 04: [Evaluating models](slides/04-evaluating-models.html){target="_blank"} - 05: [Tuning models](slides/05-tuning-models.html){target="_blank"} - 06: [Feature engineering: dummies and embeddings](slides/06-feature-engineering-part-one.html){target="_blank"} - 07: [Feature engineering: splines, target encoding and dates](slides/07-feature-engineering-part-two.html){target="_blank"} - 08: [tidymodels and LLMs](slides/08-tidymodels-and-llms.html){target="_blank"} - 09: [Wrapping up](slides/09-wrapping-up.html){target="_blank"} ### Extra content (time permitting) - [Using workflowsets](slides/extras-workflowsets.html){target="_blank"} - [Grid search via racing](slides/extras-racing.html){target="_blank"} - [Postprocessing](slides/extras-postprocessing.html){target="_blank"} - [Feature selection](slides/extras-feature-selection.html){target="_blank"} - [Transit case study (includes stacking)](slides/extras-transit-case-study.html){target="_blank"} - [Iterative search](slides/extras-iterative-search.html){target="_blank"} There's also a page for [slide annotations](slides/annotations.html){target="_blank"}; these are extra notes for selected slides. ## Code Quarto files for working along [are available on GitHub](https://github.com/tidymodels/workshops/tree/main/classwork). (Don't worry if you haven't used Quarto before; it will feel familiar to R Markdown users.) ## Past workshops ### English - [September 2025](archive/2025-09-posit-conf/index.html) at posit::conf() - [August 2025](archive/2025-08-nyr/index.html) at New York Data Science & AI Conference - [August 2024](archive/2024-08-posit-conf/index.html) at posit::conf() - [September 2023](archive/2023-09-posit-conf/) at posit::conf() - [July 2023](archive/2023-07-nyr/) at the New York R Conference - [August 2022](archive/2022-08-Reykjavik-City/) in Reykjavik - [July 2022](archive/2022-07-RStudio-conf/index.html) at [rstudio::conf()](https://posit.co/blog/talks-and-workshops-from-rstudio-conf-2022/) ### Spanish - [March 2024](archive/2024-03-conectaR-spanish/) at [conectaR](https://congresos.ucr.ac.cr/event/7/) ## Acknowledgments {.appendix} This website, including the slides, is made with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/). Please [submit an issue](https://github.com/tidymodels/workshops/issues) on the GitHub repo for this workshop if you find something that could be fixed or improved. ## Reuse and licensing {.appendix} Unless otherwise noted (i.e. not an original creation and reused from another source), these educational materials are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
